public_rationale: Related benchmarks existed well before the post, including television, movie-story, and long-video comprehension tests. They prevent treating the area as unimplemented altogether. However, the reviewed records do not establish a complete implementation with the safeguards Marcus describes. Nor can an unsuccessful search establish his universal claim that nobody had implemented it.
limitations: The boundary between a related benchmark and full implementation is not formally defined.
Public records cannot exclude undocumented implementations.
An AI's failure to pass an existing benchmark would not support the claim that the benchmark was never implemented.

our_interpretation: The historical interval runs from the June 9, 2014 proposal through the April 2, 2025 post.
A full implementation operationalizes comprehension of arbitrary audiovisual narratives, including explanations of events and characters' motives, with a scoring procedure.
The surrounding post makes protection against prior exposure and contamination part of the intended implementation.
Implementing a test does not require an AI to pass it.
Four seasons of Succession illustrates difficulty; it is not treated as a mandatory dataset.
Related video-question-answering benchmarks are candidates to examine, not automatically full implementations.
criteria.support_condition: A sufficiently comprehensive independent review establishes that no implementation meeting the stated scope and safeguards existed by the post date.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A dated implementation report, benchmark release, or evaluation protocol demonstrates that the complete challenge had been implemented by April 2, 2025.

LVBench implements long-video evaluation using public videos, multiple-choice questions, and human comparisons. These features make it a serious candidate, but the reviewed protocol does not establish the continuously refreshed, first-viewing safeguards described in the post.
